systemFindings.finding: API key delivered by Marius via confidential email; copy-paste disabled; GET against HD API returned HTTP 200 during testing but specific lead-record retrieval needed a lead F-number from Ashley.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Venkat B 2026-04-17: 'I was able to get the 200 response, but I couldn't be able to get any one specific ID. So I would require any one lead ID from your end so that I test it now and see that I am able to get the data.'

systemFindings.finding: Lead identifier is an 'F number' — not a generic numeric ID. SFIM-vendor-number is a different field that may be confused for the lead ID.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Ashley Salerno 2026-04-17: 'It says SFIM vendor. Number?' / Venkat B: 'I thought you need the lead number which is the F number.'

systemFindings.finding: Update cadence to downstream consumers is ~10 minutes (was 30 min historically).
systemFindings.sourceQuote: venkatb@dataskate.ai 2026-04-14: 'It takes ten minutes to update. Actually, on the peerless side...' / Ashley: 'A Marcos told that update every ten minutes.'

systemFindings.finding: Sandbox tenant is being provisioned by Cora Barahi (per Marius). DataSkate access pending at time of transcripts.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Raghuram Potluri 2026-04-14: 'Marius told that he will share it with us, he will create a user. He told me that Cora Barahi is going to create a user with our email and is going to share it with us for the sandbox.'

systemFindings.finding: Quote Line Item (standard object) is the canonical source for picket-type / material-type rules — no external Excel sheet needed. Picket-type determination is data-driven from product bundle (e.g. material name includes 'cedar' → wood).
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Venkat B 2026-04-15: 'this data is all available within the Salesforce. Like when you said it's a wood and correspondingly only these things should come with respect to the woods.' / Ashley: 'this object name should be Find Quote Line Item.'

systemFindings.finding: API Management menu is ONLY available in the production tenant; practice/sandbox returns 'Can't access API from practice'. Confirmed by Peerless super-admin Jean Jacobs.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Brian Cook 2026-04-17: 'wait, what did that say? Can't access API from practice.' / Jean Jacobs: 'I won't let you in practice.' / 'since the API is not available in practice, does it make sense to even create a practice ID for you or no?'

systemFindings.finding: API access requires Deltek 'CE Live Service' Windows service installed on the same VM as ComputerEase. External calls go to a Deltek-managed URL which routes back through CE Live Service to the local CE instance. Pending Deltek support ticket (filed 2026-04-17 by Jean).
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Raghuram Potluri 2026-04-17: 'these Dell tech, especially computer is APIs work in a little bit different way where like they have this CE live service installed on the same VM where we have computer is. And we have to make a call to the Dell tech URL so that they will route to our computer is instance through the CE live service.'

systemFindings.finding: ComputerEase production VM observed listening on TCP/445 (SMB) — NOT 443 or 8081. Firewall rules added for 443/8081 did not surface any service.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Brian Cook 2026-04-16: 'We're not listening on 443. We're listening on 445. Which is terrible. But that's how I'm in.'

systemFindings.finding: Single super-admin (Jean Jacobs); no backup admin. Demonstrated SPOF blocked all access changes for ~2 days during PTO.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Ashley Salerno 2026-04-16: 'The only person that does is Jean, but Laura has more access than all of us except for Jean.' / Brian Cook: 'Yeah, it's not a good practice to only have one admin, obviously for situations like this.'

systemFindings.finding: Vendor support categorises ComputerEase as legacy; minimum response SLA is 4 hours.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Brian Cook 2026-04-17: 'We're considered legacy. So, 4 hours, it won't be 2.'

systemFindings.finding: Confirmed object-set entitled to API access group at Peerless: Jobs, Subcontracts, Cost Types, Job Totals, Service Work Orders. Excluded as sensitive: Payroll, Departments, Inventory, Vendors.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Ashley Salerno 2026-04-15: 'I don't think we need payroll data... apart from payroll, if there is any confidential and classified information, let's not use that, Bharat. I think jobs is the one we needed, so you can put jobs, subcontracts.' / 'Job totals make sense.'

systemFindings.finding: ComputerEase VM has a static external IP. Pre-engagement state: SSH and RDP were open to the entire internet (no source filter); only ingress was enabled (no egress for return traffic).
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Brian Cook 2026-04-15: 'They're allowing SSH and RDP from anywhere, which is really bad practice.' / 2026-04-16: 'I'm pretty sure it is static, but it wouldn't matter right now... they're all static.'

systemFindings.finding: Cameo is the recommended interactive UI path to ComputerEase — Brian Cook explicitly preferred it over RDP because 'I don't know what guardrails are in place in Cameo or an RDP.' Cameo is NOT an integration channel.
systemFindings.sourceQuote: Brian Cook 2026-04-16: 'I would use Cameo for computer use. Unless you need to like RDP to the server to like go in and open something up on the Windows firewall, you know, of the server.'

architectKnowledge.speaker: Raghuram Potluri
architectKnowledge.finding: ComputerEase APIs are exposed via a CE Live Service Windows service on the customer VM. External callers hit a Deltek-managed URL which routes back through CE Live Service to the local CE instance. This is a legacy relay pattern, not modern REST exposure.

architectKnowledge.speaker: Raghuram Potluri
architectKnowledge.finding: Customer-managed cloud VMs hosting legacy ERPs are typically misconfigured for security (SSH/RDP open to internet, no egress rules, non-standard listening ports). Always inspect ports, firewall rules, and IP type at scoping rather than assuming standard HTTPS exposure.
architectKnowledge.system: ComputerEase / general on-prem legacy ERP on customer cloud

architectKnowledge.speaker: Raghuram Potluri
architectKnowledge.finding: Confidential / secure email tools that disable clipboard copy force credential transcription. Do NOT use an LLM to OCR a password — hallucination on a single character causes account lockout. Use a deterministic OCR tool or hand-type.

architectKnowledge.speaker: Raghuram Potluri
architectKnowledge.finding: Some legacy ERPs (ComputerEase confirmed) expose API ONLY in production — practice/sandbox tenants have no API surface at all. Agree GET-only production testing posture in writing before development.

architectKnowledge.speaker: Raghuram Potluri
architectKnowledge.finding: Principle of least privilege when given GCP access for debugging — request editor/dev role, not full admin. Demonstrated by explicitly asking Brian for editor-level GCP IAM, not super-admin, while debugging firewall rules.
architectKnowledge.writtenTo: (not promoted — single-occurrence observation, captured here only)

questionGaps.question: Does the sandbox/practice environment expose the FULL API surface, or only the UI?
Is there a designated BACKUP super-admin for this system? If not, who can we add before kickoff?
Is the API exposed directly from your VM, or through a vendor-managed relay/proxy URL?
What is the external IP of the host VM, and is it static or ephemeral?
Which TCP ports does the application listen on internally (run netstat / Get-NetTCPConnection during scoping)?
What is the lead/record identifier format and field name (e.g. F-number, GUID, integer)?
How are API credentials delivered? Confidential email with clipboard disabled? If so, plan transcription buffer and do NOT OCR passwords via LLM.
What is the vendor's support SLA, and is the product classified 'legacy' (= slower SLA)?
Is the ERP on the vendor's cloud, or on a customer-managed cloud VM? If customer-managed: who owns firewall rules, IAM, and uptime?
Are there sequential identifier policies (job number, invoice number) that prevent test writes from taking the next-in-line ID?
